bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 12241: harfbuzz has a reported memory-safety bug. Crash Type: Heap-double-free at 0x619000000080. Crash State: hb_vector_t<CFF::op_str_t, 8u>::fini -> hb_vector_t<CFF::cff1_font_dict_values_t, 8u>::~hb_vector_t -> OT::cff1::accelerator_templ_t::~accelerator_templ_t. Sanitizer: AddressSanitizer. Fuzz target: hb-subset-fuzzer. The subset planner initializes a CFF1 accelerator over an attacker-controlled font; the CFF1 font-dict vector reallocates from its inline pre-allocated store to the heap with a shallow byte copy that duplicates owning sub-vector pointers, and the parsed op-string buffers are then freed twice.

source.description: The CFF1 accelerator references (materializes) the raw CFF table blob out of the attacker-controlled font face; this project-level input load is the scored source that supplies the untrusted CFF byte stream later interpreted into font-dict op-strings.
source.value_from: The untrusted font file supplied to hb-subset-fuzzer is loaded into an hb_face_t; reference_table<cff1>(face) materializes the raw CFF table bytes as `blob` from `this->blob = sc.reference_table<cff1> (face);`.

sink.description: ASan reports the double-free here: during the automatic destruction of the CFF1FontDictValues vector's inline static_array (~hb_vector_t at line 44, invoked by ~accelerator_templ_t at hb-ot-cff1-table.hh:1010), the op-string buffer of a stale bytewise copy is free()'d a second time, having already been freed by the earlier fini_deep().

root_cause.description: When the CFF1FontDictValues vector grows past its inline PreallocedCount and migrates from `static_array` to a fresh heap buffer, alloc() performs a shallow bytewise memcpy of the elements. CFF1FontDictValues is non-trivially-copyable (it owns an hb_vector_t<OpStr>), so the copy duplicates each element's owning op-string pointer into the heap buffer while the identical (now aliased) pointers remain in `static_array`. fini_deep() later frees the op-string buffers through the heap copies, and the subsequent automatic destruction of the stale `static_array` elements frees the same buffers again -> heap double-free. The fix commit reduces PreallocedCount from 8 to 2 (hb-vector.hh:35) to shrink/avoid this inline-store-to-heap migration double-free window.

parser_admitted.description: The input has passed CFF table admission (blob->as<cff1>() non-null, name/top-dict indices sanitized) and been dispatched onto the CID-keyed path, where fdCount is taken from the attacker-controlled FDArray; the per-font-dict interpretation loop that allocates and later double-frees the op-string buffers is now entered.

tainted_value_origin.description: Each CID font dict is interpreted from the attacker-controlled fontDictStr into a CFF1FontDictValues pushed onto the fontDicts vector; the interpretation populates the owning hb_vector_t<OpStr> (via add_op) whose backing buffer is the object that is ultimately double-freed.

coarse_trace.summary: Subset planner constructs a CFF1 accelerator over the attacker-controlled font (cff.init(face)).
References the CFF table blob and dispatches onto the CID font-dict parsing path.
Interpreting each font dict pushes op-strings, heap-allocating the OpStr backing buffer.
The font-dict vector migrates from its inline static_array to the heap via a shallow memcpy, aliasing each element's owning op-string pointer.
An init error path calls fini(); fontDicts.fini_deep() frees the op-string buffers through the heap copies (first free).
The accelerator's scope-exit destructor destroys the stale static_array copies, freeing the same op-string buffers a second time (double-free).

fine_trace.note: Scored source: the raw CFF table bytes are materialized from the attacker-controlled font face into `blob`.
The CFF table is cast/admitted from the loaded blob; name index and top dict index are sanitized before dispatch.

Parser-admission checkpoint: the CID-keyed path is taken and the number of font dicts to parse is read from the attacker-controlled FDArray. When fdCount exceeds the vector's inline PreallocedCount the later fontDicts growth migrates to the heap.
For each i in [0, fdCount) the attacker-controlled font-dict byte string is materialized from the FDArray.
A new CFF1FontDictValues slot is pushed onto the fontDicts vector. The push that first drives len past PreallocedCount triggers the static_array-to-heap reallocation (step 8).
The font dict is interpreted from fontDictStr, populating font's owning hb_vector_t<OpStr> via add_op. This is the value whose backing buffer is double-freed.
Interpretation appends parsed operators/operands, growing the OpStr `values` vector.
The OpStr `values` vector heap-allocates its backing buffer (the 912-byte region ASan later double-frees). This buffer becomes owned by a CFF1FontDictValues element stored in the fontDicts vector.

ROOT CAUSE (aliasing): when fontDicts grows past PreallocedCount it migrates from the inline static_array to `new_array` with a shallow bytewise memcpy. Each CFF1FontDictValues owns an hb_vector_t<OpStr>, so its op-string pointer (from step 8) is duplicated into the heap buffer while the identical pointer stays in the stale static_array element. Two owners of one buffer now exist. The fix reduces PreallocedCount 8->2 (hb-vector.hh:35) to shrink this migration window.

A subsequent sanitize/interpret failure on the CID path takes a `{ fini (); return; }` branch. accelerator::fini() calls fontDicts.fini_deep(), which iterates the heap copies (arrayZ()) and frees each element's op-string buffer via hb_vector_t<OpStr>::fini (hb-vector.hh:72 -> 63). FIRST free. The stale static_array copies are NOT visited and keep their now-dangling op-string pointers.

SINK (double-free): at scope exit the accelerator's ~accelerator_templ_t (hb-ot-cff1-table.hh:1010) destroys the fontDicts member; ~hb_vector_t<CFF1FontDictValues> (hb-vector.hh:44) auto-destructs the inline static_array elements, whose stale op-string pointers (aliased at step 9, already freed at step 10) are free()'d again here. ASan aborts with heap-double-free on 0x619000000080.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: partial: the crash/free and the aliasing reallocation are both in hb-vector.hh; the allocation_context (line 174) is the OpStr buffer alloc, while the root-cause aliasing memcpy is the CFF1FontDictValues static->heap migration at line 168

format.name: CFF-flavored OpenType/TrueType font (CID-keyed CFF1)
format.contract: Candidate input must be admitted as an sfnt/OpenType font carrying a CFF ('CFF ') table that hb-subset loads via hb_face_t, so accelerator_templ_t::init parses it. The CFF top dict must sanitize and select the CID-keyed path (valid FDArray/FDSelect), and the FDArray must declare enough font dicts (count exceeding the hb_vector_t inline PreallocedCount) that the fontDicts vector reallocates from its inline static_array to the heap while at least one font dict interprets into a non-empty op-string vector, then a later per-font-dict sanitize/interpret step must fail so init takes a fini() error path. Preserving CFF-table admission, the CID FDArray structure, and the reallocation-inducing font-dict count is what keeps a candidate reachability-comparable.
